title: Approval of immobilizers and approval of a vehicle with regard to its immobilizer
scope_summary: Approves immobilizers, as devices intended to be permanently fitted to vehicles of any category, and approves vehicles with regard to their immobilizer(s). Vehicle approval covers category M1 and N1 with a maximum mass of not more than 2 tonnes, extendable to other categories at the manufacturer's request; only 12 V electrical systems are considered.
scope_quote: 1.1 Approval of immobilizers which are intended to be permanently fitted to vehicles of any category. 1.2 Approval of vehicles of category M1 and those of category N1 with a maximum mass of not more than 2 tonnes, with regard to their immobilizer(s). 1.3 At the request of the manufacturer, Contracting Parties may grant approvals to vehicles of other categories with regard to their immobilizer(s). 1.4 This UN Regulation does not apply to radio transmission frequencies, whether or not related to the protection of vehicles against unauthorized use.
vehicle_categories: Any category (immobilizer as component/separate technical unit)
N1 (maximum mass not more than 2 tonnes)
Other categories at manufacturer's request (vehicle approval)
Only vehicles with 12 V electrical systems
relation_to_other_regulations: Combined approval as immobilizer under R162 and alarm system under UN Regulation No. [ZZZ], UN R116 (Supplement 7 to the original version) or UN R97 (Supplement 8 to the 01 series): both approval marks affixed to the major element(s) of the device (para. 4.8).

An immobilizer approved as a separate technical unit to R162, UN R116 (Supplement 7 to original version) or UN R97 (Supplement 8 to 01 series) installed in a vehicle submitted for R162 approval need not repeat immobilizer tests (para. 4.11).
Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6.
Does not cover radio transmission frequencies (para. 1.4).

defined_terms.definition: A device subject to the requirements of this regulation, intended to be part of a vehicle, which may be type-approved independently of a vehicle where the regulation expressly provides.
A device subject to this regulation, intended to be part of a vehicle, which may be type-approved separately but only in relation to one or more specified vehicle types.
A device which is intended to prevent normal driving away of a vehicle under its own power (prevention of unauthorized use).
Equipment necessary for the setting and/or unsetting of an immobilizer.
Any device intended to indicate the status of the immobilizer (set/unset, change of set to unset and vice versa).
The state in which the vehicle cannot be driven normally under its own power.
The state in which the vehicle can be driven normally.
Any mechanical and/or electronic solution designed and constructed to provide a method of operating a locking system designed to be operated by that solution.
A design feature which locks the immobilizer in the unset condition.
An electronic code of several elements whose combination changes at random after each operation of the transmitting unit.
Systems not differing significantly in trade name or mark, kind of control equipment, and design of their operation on the relevant vehicle system(s).

defined_terms.term: Vehicle type with regard to its immobilizer
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing significantly in trade name or mark, vehicle features significantly influencing immobilizer performance, and type and design of the immobilizer.
A user who is able to authorize digital keys; there can be more than one.
A key designed to be transferred to multiple devices by the primary user(s) through dedicated processes.
A distance of less than 6 m.

applicability_hints: Aftermarket immobilizers intended to be permanently fitted fall under the component approval regardless of vehicle category.
Smartphone/phone-as-key or shareable keys count as 'digital keys' and trigger Annex 9 (documentation, cyber-attack resistance, verification).
Key fobs, transponder keys, keypads or cards used to set/unset the immobilizer are 'control equipment' and/or 'keys' within this regulation.
Indicator LEDs or displays showing immobilizer status are 'status displays'.
Integrated vehicle alarm/immobilizer units may need dual approval with R116, R97 or the alarm regulation; a prior STU approval under R116/R97 avoids retesting.
Immobilizer components must meet EMC immunity/emission tests in Annex 7 and environmental/vibration tests in Annex 6.
Radio transmission frequencies of remote controls are outside scope.
Only 12 V electrical systems are considered.
